items.headline: Belgium's airports shut for a day as air traffic control joins an anti-austerity strike
items.summary: Skeyes suspends services from 07:00 to 21:00 local time, so nearly all flights are cancelled and only emergency and safety-critical flights continue.
items.matters: it is the 11th strike to hit Belgian airspace in 11 months, with a large Brussels demonstration planned. PM Bart De Wever is still trying to agree a budget that saves €10bn after offering his resignation in early November, which the King rejected.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info A view of Brussels airport, Belgium, on November 6, 2026 [Geert Vanden Wijngaert/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and DPA Published On 23 Nov 2026 23 Nov 2026 Nearly all flights are set to be cancelled in Belgium on Monday after the country’s air traffic controller said its staff would take part in a national strike against government austerity measures.

Skeyes, the company responsible for Belgium’s air traffic control, said it would be unable to provide regular services at the country’s airports and in its airspace between 7am (06:00 GMT) and 9pm (20:00 GMT) on Monday.

The Brussels-Charleroi airport, a major European hub for low-cost airline Ryanair, said the strike would result in the “complete shutdown of all the country’s airports for an entire day”, affecting thousands of passengers.

“Without air traffic control, no flights can take off or land,” the Brussels-Charleroi airport said, criticising a “last-minute decision” with “disastrous consequences”.

Belgian unions have called for a nationwide day of action on Monday to protest against austerity and reform measures pursued by the country’s governing coalition.

The Board of Airline Representatives in Belgium, which represents about 25 carriers, said the walkout would be the 11th strike affecting Belgian airspace in 11 months.

The unions also plan a large-scale demonstration in Brussels on Monday. Significant disruption is expected to public transport, while schools, government offices and refuse collection services may also be affected.

Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has been in protracted talks with his coalition partners on a cost-cutting budget that will save 10 billion euros ($11bn) over the next few years by Monday, in a bid to reduce the country’s high deficit.

Earlier in November, De Wever offered his resignation after his coalition failed to reach a deal. However, Belgium’s King Philippe rejected the resignation and gave the prime minister more time to find a solution.

items.headline: Israel's Likud–Yashar unity talks end without a deal
items.summary: Netanyahu's party and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc met in Herzliya on Sunday and disagreed over who leads the government and whether Itamar Ben-Gvir joins. A follow-up meeting is planned with no date.
items.matters: Eisenkot has until 6 December, with a possible 14-day extension, and his bloc is 13 seats short of a majority after winning 48 in October. The fallback is a minority government that would need outside support from Arab parties.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info An election billboard in Tel Aviv shows caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, left, and leader of the Yashar party, Gadi Eisenkot [File: Abir Sultan/EPA] By Al Jazeera Staff, Anadolu and AP Published On 22 Nov 2026 22 Nov 2026 Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.

In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.

Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.

Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.

However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.

If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

items.headline: Nadzwyczajne posiedzenie Rady Północnoatlantyckiej odbywa się dziś, a Polska wyśle też szefa kontrwywiadu wojskowego
items.summary: wiceminister obrony Paweł Zalewski i gen. bryg. Jarosław Stróżyk z SKW mają przedstawić sojusznikom „bardzo konkretne" propozycje wzmocnienia obrony powietrznej wschodniej flanki oraz informacje o rakietach, które spadły w Polsce.
items.matters: Polska nie będzie wnioskować o artykuł 4, bo według Zalewskiego Sojusz już chroni wschodnią flankę, a Kosiniak-Kamysz poprosił wcześniej o samoloty AWACS i wsparcie sojuszniczych F-35.
items.body:
Dziś w kwaterze głównej NATO w Brukseli odbędzie się nadzwyczajne posiedzenie Rady Północnoatlantyckiej w związku z naruszeniem polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej przez rosyjskie obiekty. Jak ustaliło RMF FM, Polskę będą reprezentować nie tylko wiceminister obrony narodowej Paweł Zalewski, ale także szef Służby Kontrwywiadu Wojskowego, generał brygady Jarosław Stróżyk. Ma on przedstawić sojusznikom informacje dotyczące rakiet, które spadły na terytorium Polski oraz zagrożeń ze strony Rosji.

Generał brygady Jarosław Stróżyk (fot. Wojciech Olkuśnik) / East News Polska przedstawi konkretne propozycje Zalewski zapowiedział w rozmowie z RMF FM, że Polska przedstawi konkretne propozycje wzmocnienia obrony powietrznej wschodniej flanki NATO.

Będę mówił o rzeczach bardzo konkretnych – zapewnił wiceminister. Polska chce również przedstawić stanowisko rządu w sprawie ostatnich wydarzeń i uzyskać jednoznaczne poparcie Sojuszu.

Pytany o szczegóły planowanego wzmocnienia ochrony polskiego nieba, wiceminister zaznaczył, że nie chce wykraczać poza informacje, które wcześniej przedstawił szef MON Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Ten zwrócił się do sojuszników o samoloty wczesnego ostrzegania AWACS oraz wsparcie w postaci sojuszniczych myśliwców F-35.

Mówimy tutaj o AWACS-ach, mówimy tutaj również o bardzo poważnych zdolnościach lotniczych, ale nie tylko. Ja o szczegółach, poza tymi, które przedstawił pan premier Kosiniak-Kamysz, nie będę mówił – zaznaczył Zalewski.

Warszawa nie zamierza wnioskować o uruchomienie artykułu 4. Traktatu Północnoatlantyckiego, przewidującego konsultacje sojusznicze w przypadku zagrożenia bezpieczeństwa jednego z państw członkowskich. Jak tłumaczy Zalewski, nie ma takiej potrzeby, ponieważ Sojusz już prowadzi działania na rzecz ochrony wschodniej flanki, a polską przestrzeń powietrzną chronią również siły sojusznicze.

Spotkanie odbędzie się na szczeblu ambasadorów państw NATO. Udział w nim polskiego wiceministra obrony i szefa kontrwywiadu wojskowego ma podkreślić wagę sprawy. Po zakończeniu posiedzenia głos zabierze sekretarz generalny NATO Mark Rutte.

items.headline: Dziś kończy się trzyletnie zamrożenie skarg na „neosędziów" w Strasburgu
items.summary: Europejski Trybunał Praw Człowieka rozpatrywał dotąd wstrzymane sprawy od 23 listopada 2023, a czeka ich ponad 1200.
items.matters: reform sądownictwa, których domagał się wyrok w sprawie Wałęsa przeciwko Polsce, nie przeprowadzono, więc grozi fala przegranych spraw i wysokich odszkodowań, a MSZ nie skomentowało, czy Polska prosiła o przedłużenie.
items.body:
Skomentuj W poniedziałek mija termin, na który Europejski Trybunał Praw Człowieka zamroził rozpatrywanie skarg złożonych przeciwko Polsce na wyroki wydane z udziałem neosędziów - informuje poniedziałkowy „Dziennik Gazeta Prawna”. Na rozpatrzenie czeka ponad 1,2 tys. skarg, a spodziewane są kolejne.

fot. CherryX / / Wikimedia Commons Ich zawieszenie miało dać rządowi czas na uporządkowanie wymiaru sprawiedliwości po zmianach wprowadzonych przez PiS. Choć początkowo było planowane na rok, a ostatecznie potrwało trzy lata, Polsce nie udało się wprowadzić reform. A to oznacza, że nasz kraj musi się liczyć z masowym przegrywaniem spraw oraz koniecznością wypłaty ogromnych odszkodowań - pisze gazeta.

Biuro prasowe ETPC nie odpowiedziało na pytania „DGP” dotyczące tego, czy ze strony polskiego rządu wpłynął wniosek, by obowiązujące od 23 listopada 2023 r. zawieszenie przedłużyć raz jeszcze. Do sprawy nie odniosło się też Ministerstwo Spraw Zagranicznych, które odpowiada za reprezentację Polski przed ETPC.

Gazeta przypomina, że systemową dysfunkcję polskiego sądownictwa stwierdzono w wyroku z 23 listopada 2023 r. w sprawie Wałęsa przeciwko Polsce, będącej pokłosiem orzeczenia Izby Kontroli Nadzwyczajnej i Spraw Publicznych Sądu Najwyższego, która po ponad 10 latach uchyliła prawomocny wyrok w sprawie naruszenia dóbr osobistych byłego prezydenta przez nazywanie go agentem SB.

Na podstawie art. 46 Europejskiej Konwencji Praw Człowieka trybunał nałożył wówczas na Polskę obowiązek przyjęcia pilnych środków legislacyjnych i organizacyjnych obejmujących m.in. reformę Krajowej Rady Sądownictwa, uregulowanie statusu sędziów powołanych przy udziale wadliwie obsadzonej KRS oraz reformę instytucji skargi nadzwyczajnej.

items.headline: Prezes CPK zapowiada możliwe opóźnienia przetargu na terminal Portu Polska
items.summary: Piotr Borys mówi w „Pulsie Biznesu", że projekty wymagają korekt, a przegląd dokumentacji zakończy się w styczniu 2027.
items.matters: wykonawcy złożyli odwołania i chcą więcej czasu, ale Borys podtrzymuje cel 2032, jeśli oferty wpłyną na początku przyszłego roku, a koszt terminala i infrastruktury lotniska szacuje na ponad 43 mld zł.
items.body:
Skomentuj Projekty związane z budową Portu Polska wymagają korekt, a inwestycje koordynacji - mówi w wywiadzie dla poniedziałkowego „Pulsu Biznesu” Piotr Borys, prezes CPK.

/ CPK W styczniu 2027 r. zakończy się przegląd dokumentacji. Wówczas dowiemy się, czy gigalotnisko powstanie do 2032 r. W tej chwili ten termin wciąż jest aktualny, choć najpewniej przesunięta zostanie data składania ofert na budowę - pisze gazeta.

Uruchomione zostały w trybie dialogu konkurencyjnego przetargi na terminal. Wpłynęły odwołania wykonawców, a także sygnały o konieczności wyznaczenia dłuższego terminu na otwarcie ofert. „ Wyciągamy wnioski z postępowań, by uniknąć problemów podczas kolejnych przetargów - zakładam więc, że obecny termin będzie przesunięty ” - mówi Piotr Borys.

Nie sprecyzował, jaki będzie nowy termin. „ Będziemy dążyć do tego, by jak najmniej przesuwać terminy, ale skoro mamy wyraźny sygnał, że trzeba je zmienić, to musimy je przeanalizować ” - stwierdził. Zaznaczył przy tym, że w każdym dużym projekcie zmienia się około 20 proc. zakresu inwestycji.

Na pytanie, czy z obecnego przetargu na terminal mogą zostać wyłączone systemy bezpieczeństwa, odparł: „W tej chwili zakres pozostaje bez zmian, ale nie wykluczam, że w tak długim procesie nastąpią skoki technologiczne wymagające modyfikacji niektórych założeń - np. właśnie w obszarze bezpieczeństwa”.

Zdaniem Piotra Borysa dotrzymanie terminu zakończenia budowy w 2032 r. nadal jest możliwe. „Zakładamy, że jeśli złożenie ofert nastąpi na początku przyszłego roku, np. w lutym, to przy odpowiedniej organizacji działań dotrzymanie terminu nadal jest możliwe” - powiedział.

items.headline: Central banks are lining up December hikes
items.summary: Bankier says markets price 100% for a Fed hike on 9 December, about 95% for a third ECB quarter-point hike on 17 December and a Bank of Japan move to 1.50% on 18 December.
items.matters: Bankier notes that Brent is more than 20% cheaper than a month ago and European gas fell from nearly €104/MWh to about €82.5/MWh, so these could be the last hikes of the cycle if core inflation does not rise.
items.body:
Skomentuj Jeszcze przed Bożym Narodzeniem najważniejsze banki centralne świata prawdopodobnie zdecydują się na kolejną rundę podwyżek stóp procentowych. I być może kolejnej już nie będzie.

fot. BRENDAN MCDERMID / / Reuters Przynajmniej do końca października światowa gospodarka najprawdopodobniej znajdowała się w inflacyjnej fazie ożywienia gospodarczego. W górę szły zarówno dynamiki PKB jak i inflacji CPI. Nieco wcześniej – bo jeszcze w połowie września – blisko 20-letnie maksimum ustanowił surowcowy indeks CRB. Także we wrześniu swoje 40-miesięczne maksimum ustanowił globalny wskaźnik PMI opracowywany przez bank JP Morgan Chase. Co więcej, jest możliwe, że na przełomie września i października zobaczyliśmy cykliczny szczyt rentowności obligacji skarbowyc h. Przypomnę tylko, że 10-letnie Treasuries oferowały wtedy nawet 5,366% rentowności w terminie do wykupu.

Puls Biznesu Będąca prawdopodobnie już w znacznej mierze za nami inflacyjna faza ożywienia gospodarczego premiowała inwestycje w surowce (a zwłaszcza akcje spółek surowcowych) oraz bardzo brutalnie obeszła się z obligacjami i stałym kuponie. Faza ta kończy się wtedy, gdy tempo wzrostu PKB osiąga swoje cykliczne maksimum. W przypadku Polski niemal na pewno ten punkt jest już albo za nami, albo pojawi się on w bieżącym, IV kwartale 2026 roku.

Po osiągnięciu cyklicznego minimum wzrost gospodarczy będzie malał, ale inflacja cenowa może jeszcze przez kilka miesięcy rosnąć – napędzana choćby efektami niskiej, zeszłorocznej bazy. Szanse realizacji tego scenariusza rosną za sprawą wyraźnego złagodzenia napięć na rynkach surowcowych. Przecież ropa Brent jest teraz o ponad 20% tańsza, niż była jeszcze niespełna miesiąc temu. Giełdowe notowania benzyny zdążyły w tym czasie spaść niemal o jedną trzecią, a oleju napędowego o 1/5. To samo dotyczy też giełdowych cen gazu ziemnego w Europie, który jeszcze pod koniec października sięgały niemal 104€ za MWh, a w chwili pisania tego artykułu wnosiły ok. 82,5€.

Tym razem bankierzy centralni w większości nie chowali głów w piasku i wbrew podręcznikom ekonomii na klasyczny szok podażowy (czyli pojawienie się niedoborów surowcowych) zareagowali umiarkowanym zacieśnieniem polityki monetarnej. Od początku 2026 roku stopy procentowe poszły w górę w 38 krajach. Wśród największych gospodarek świata trend ten zainicjował Bank Rezerw Australii, który podniósł stopy jeszcze w lutym. W ślad za Australijczykami poszli inni. Europejski Bank Centralny podniósł stopy dwa razy (obie podwyżki o 25 pb.). Później dołączyli bankierzy centralni z Czech, Banku Anglii, Banku Japonii,…

items.headline: Chinese attackers used AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day without human direction
items.summary: Amazon's CISO CJ Moses says the agents ran the open-source Cairn framework and found a path-traversal flaw in MONAI Label, a medical imaging AI app. They then took over a university server in East Asia and ran a root reverse shell, "adapting for nearly a full day without human direction".
items.matters: the project has published a fix after Amazon's notification, and it is a documented case of autonomous exploitation in the wild.
items.body:
Suspected Chinese spies deployed AI agents which worked autonomously to find a zero-day in an open source application and then abuse the flaw to break into university networks, gaining full control of a server, according to Amazon CISO CJ Moses.

The China-linked attacker used Cairn, an open source, penetration-testing framework that has become increasingly popular with cybercriminals who use the AI tool to carry out multi-stage intrusions with no human assistance.

In this case, the agents found and exploited a zero-day MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application. Amazon notified the project's maintainers of the vulnerability, and they released a fix and a security advisory.

On September 10, Amazon's Threat Intelligence Team found a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn that provided visibility into the campaign targeting universities in East Asia, outside Mainland China, Moses said in a Friday report shared with The Register.

The campaign occurred over a period of 48 hours beginning on September 8, and the prompts were written in Simplified Chinese, with timestamps in executed scripts configured to China Standard Time.

Before the AI agents found and exploited the zero day, however, they tried to break into another university’s Redis server over about 16 hours and 148 sequential actions, including abusing Redis's replication feature to load unauthorized code, escaping its scripting sandbox, writing to its configuration files, and corrupting its memory.

None of these were successful, and when those actions failed, the agents also attempted a Log4Shell injection against a different service, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack against a vulnerability in a co-located Qdrant instance, and several credential sprays against PostgreSQL, SSH, and other tools.

Meanwhile, a separate operation running for more than 6 hours targeted a university GPU server with another credential-spray attack, compiling a list of 80 real user names found across the school’s public websites, academic papers and other documents.

"Neither operation succeeded, yet together they show that the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction," Moses wrote.

Then the AI agents found the zero-day path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label, and this time they were able to gain access to the server.

items.headline: GL.iNet's cloud management flaw is being used to infect routers and KVM devices
items.summary: attackers abused the GoodCloud service to install malware that hides itself and opens root reverse shells. RemoteToHome found suspicious activity on 152 of the 183 routers it checked, and some recovered files date from December 2025.
items.matters: GL.iNet says new infections through this path are blocked but existing malware is not removed. KVM owners need firmware 1.10.3 or later (1.8.7 for the RMQ1), and some devices may need a clean reinstall.
items.body:
GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access to infected devices.

GL.iNet manufactures networking equipment, including home and travel routers, as well as KVM devices that allow users to access and control computers remotely.

Its GoodCloud platform allows customers to remotely manage supported devices, including accessing and controlling computers and servers connected to its KVM products.

In a security advisory published on November 20, GL.iNet confirmed that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to access devices and install malicious software.

"The attack path has been blocked. We fixed the cloud vulnerability and blocked the access used in this incident," the company said.

"Devices can no longer be newly infected through this attack path. These measures do not remove malware from devices that were already infected."

GL.iNet has not disclosed how the attackers exploited its cloud platform, how many customers were impacted, or whether information was stolen from compromised devices.

The company's initial instructions told customers to look for a process running as crond -i /tmp/.log, which GL.iNet said was an indicator of compromise.

While the cloud vulnerability has been fixed, GL.iNet says stable firmware updates containing additional security fixes for both routers and KVM devices are scheduled for release on November 22, 2026.

For KVM devices, customers can follow the company's firmware upgrade guidance, which recommends version 1.10.3 or later for the RM10, RM1, RM1V2, RM1PE, and RM4PE, version 1.10.3 beta or later for the RM10RC, and version 1.8.7 or later for the RMQ1.

OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development Anthony Ha 1:14 PM PST · November 22, 2026 A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.

A tale of two Nvidias Anthony Ha 1:07 PM PST · November 21, 2026 Listen on Apple Podcasts Listen on Spotify We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no plans for Huang to return.

Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.

What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.

A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.

Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China.

And again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line.

Kirsten: Although Nvidia’s bottom line is doing just fine. In every possible way, their guidance was incredible. They beat expectations. They have a long pipeline.

It was really interesting because you have that happening, and then you have all this noise happening in social media, and also a number of other tech conferences were happening this past week — Dealbook Summit, there [were] a few others in which you had the highest profile people that you can think of in the tech world…

items.headline: F5 ships emergency patches for five critical BIG-IP flaws
items.summary: the unauthenticated stack overflows affect Access Policy Manager and iRules and can crash the traffic microkernel or give remote code execution. F5 says none of them is exploited yet.
items.matters: F5 offers no mitigations, only the hotfixes. Shadowserver counts more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances online, and a September APM flaw was exploited as a zero-day.
items.body:
US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution.

Tracked as CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, and CVE-2026-123637, these stack-based buffer overflow flaws affect the company's BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) centralized access management proxy solution and the BIG-IP iRules programmable scripting feature.

All five security issues are rated critical severity, and unauthenticated threat actors can exploit them to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) and execute arbitrary code remotely on systems with vulnerable configurations.

The company also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability (CVE-2026-126822) stemming from an integer underflow (wrap or wraparound) weakness that remote, unauthenticated threat actors can abuse in denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.

"Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may perform RCE," F5 said. "There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only."

F5 said it has no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday to address them on vulnerable devices.

Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver currently tracks more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances and over 14,600 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online. However, there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been patched against these vulnerabilities.

Although the company hasn't flagged any of these issues as exploited in attacks, admins should upgrade systems to the latest version as soon as possible, since cybercrime and nation-state threat groups have often abused F5 vulnerabilities in the wild.

Attackers have targeted F5 security flaws to breach corporate networks, map internal servers, hijack devices, deploy data-wiping malware, and steal sensitive files from victims worldwide in recent years.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged seven F5 vulnerabilities as actively exploited since November 2021, four of them also used by ransomware gangs.

Most recently, in September, F5 also patched a critical BIG-IP APM vulnerability (CVE-2026-94127) that is being actively exploited in zero-day remote code execution attacks.

items.headline: .NET 11 is out, with C# 15 union types
items.summary: it is a Standard Term Support release with two years of support, and .NET 10 stays the supported LTS option. C# 15 adds union types, closed class hierarchies, collection-expression arguments, extension indexers and labeled break/continue.
items.matters: .NET 8 and .NET 9 reached end of support on 10 November, and Runtime Async is an opt-in preview with `runtime-async=on`.
items.body:
Today, we’re excited to announce the release of.NET 11! This year’s release makes building modern applications faster, more productive, and has improvements across C# 15, ASP.NET Core,.NET MAUI, and Windows development. With hundreds of runtime optimizations, more responsive SDK tooling, and less overhead in everyday commands, you can spend less time waiting and more time creating. Build richer web and cross-platform applications, take advantage of new C# language features, and explore AI-powered development with improved tools and agentic capabilities.

Explore.NET 11 with the product teams and community at.NET Conf 2026. The conference includes product team sessions on November 10 and 11, followed by two days of community sessions.

The what’s new in.NET 11 overview links to the full details. Here are the changes behind those headlines and how to start using them.

C# 15 is the default language version for projects targeting.NET 11. Union types are one of its biggest additions: a value can be one of a declared set of case types, with conversions from those types and exhaustiveness checking in switch expressions.

Consider a product lookup that either finds a product or reports that it wasn’t found:

ProductLookup result = new Product(42, "Mechanical keyboard"); string message = result switch { Product product => $"Found {product.Name}", ProductNotFound missing => $"No product with ID {missing.Id}", }; Console.WriteLine(message); public sealed record Product(int Id, string Name); public sealed record ProductNotFound(int Id); public union ProductLookup(Product, ProductNotFound); The result type tells a caller which outcomes it needs to handle. There’s no need to use object or an unrelated base class just to put those outcomes behind one return type.

C# 15 also adds closed hierarchies. A closed class limits direct derivation to its declaring assembly, giving the compiler the information it needs to check patterns over the hierarchy. Unions are useful when you want to combine existing types; closed hierarchies fit models where you own the inheritance relationship.

Smaller language features help with everyday code, too. Collection expression arguments let you pass constructor or factory arguments without giving up collection expression syntax:

HashSet<string> names = [with(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase), "Alice", "ALICE", "Bob"]; Console.WriteLine(names.Count); This prints 2: the comparer controls equality, so "Alice" and "ALICE" are one entry.

items.headline: Blizzard wants to "get rid of BiS" in raid itemization
items.summary: Senior Game Designer Aidan Moon said on the Forever podcast that items will carry unique effects against certain creature types or in certain biomes.
items.matters: raids span several biomes and boss types, so min-maxers may need different gear per boss, and Blizzard plans bigger bags and better item sorting to cope.
items.body:
Following a general discussion of flavor items in WoW Forever in this week’s episode of the WoW Forever Podcast, Senior Game Designer Aidan Moon, AKA Zirene, went on to talk about how the developers are approaching endgame gearing. He said their goal is to make itemization more interesting and complex so players aren’t encouraged to chase down an exact best-in-slot item for each slot and ignore everything else.

One way they’re trying to change that is by adding more items that have unique effects against certain types of creatures or in certain biomes. Raids will often have different biomes in different parts of the instance as well as different types of bosses. Ultimately, players may be prioritizing completely different gear for each boss if they want to truly min/max.

Obviously this means that players will be carrying a lot more items around, but the developers are planning to expand bags to account for that and generally improve inventory and item sorting.

Add Stereogum to Google Concertgoers were evacuated from Don Toliver’s show at Co-op Live tonight after an unknown substance believed to be tear gas was released in the crowd. Social media videos from the Manchester venue show fans coughing and covering their faces during “TORE UP,” midway through the planned set. Toliver left the stage during “K9” and did not return. “Due to unforeseen circumstances, the show is now finished,” a Co-op Live representative said after the lights came on. Greater Manchester Police arrived on the scene with emergency crews including the Hazardous Area Response Team as over 12,000 people were evacuated.

"Anyone at last night's event who has since noticed side-effects or become ill should attend their local hospital," GMP say in a statement. "Enquiries are underway into what the substance is and what caused the incident."

In May 2017, 22 people were killed in a terrorist attack at nearby AO Arena (then Manchester Arena) following an Ariana Grande concert. Tonight, police declared a “major incident” at Co-op Live, but reported no serious injuries. The North West Ambulance Service said at least one attendee was taken to the hospital for assessment.

I feel horrible about what happened on Thursday after the show. I'm sorry to all the fans & supporters who got hurt, & who were scared. I wasn't aware that the merch was next to the exit, & most importantly I wasn't aware of the power behind my words. Im taking this time to take a step back & reflect & learn from this situation. I'll prioritize safety over excitement moving forward. & to the 4 people who got hurt, I personally want to apologize to you.

Based on videos and statements posted online, it looked like horrifying chaos. There was also an alleged burst pipe and reports of the fire alarm going off. Fans also reported intense crowd pushing and people passing out.

items.headline: Netflix orders a US remake of Harlan Coben's The Innocent
items.summary: Netflix calls it its 15th Coben adaptation, and the series order came this month with no cast announced.
items.matters: What's on Netflix counts five more Coben projects in the works, including The Woods (UK) in the first half of 2027 and the US Myron Bolitar series in 2027, while The Innocent itself is expected in 2028.
items.body:
Following the record-breaking success of 'I Will Find You,' Netflix has at least five more Harlan Coben adaptations in the works.

Harlan Coben’s partnership with Netflix shows no signs of slowing down. With thirteen series already streaming and I Will Find You now sitting among the biggest English-language shows in Netflix history, the streamer has five more Coben projects in the works, plus a brand-new podcast. Here’s your complete guide to everything coming soon from Harlan Coben on Netflix in 2027 and beyond, including the UK adaptation of The Woods, the highly anticipated Myron Bolitar series, the newly announced English-language remake of The Innocent, and Coben’s own podcast, What’s Your Plot Twist?

Coben first signed with Netflix in 2018 in a deal that originally ran through 2023 before being renewed in 2022. At the time, Coben stated on the record that his initial plans would bring him up to “nine of the planned 14 when the deal was struck.” He has now well surpassed that projection, with Netflix billing the newly announced remake of The Innocent as its 15th Coben adaptation. The Myron Bolitar novels were notably excluded from the deal initially struck but have been included from 2022 onwards.

Coben is deeply involved with all the Netflix titles through his production company, Final Twist Productions, and is listed as an executive producer on each project at a minimum.

Looking to catch up on what’s already streaming first? Head over to our guide on how to watch the Harlan Coben series on Netflix in order, or see how we’ve ranked all 13 series.

Note: Listed in order of likely release date, either by production dates or priority at Netflix. Everything is subject to change.

Following the 2020 Polish adaptation of the same novel, The Woods is being adapted for a second time as a brand-new UK-based thriller. The 8-part limited series is helmed by lead writer and executive producer Danny Brocklehurst and produced by Quay Street Productions, with Andy De Emmony, Claire Tailyour, and Isher Sahota directing.

The story follows Paul ‘Cope’ Copeland (Tom Bateman), a top barrister and devoted single father whose life was torn apart 20 years ago when his sister Camille vanished from a summer camp. After a body turns up seemingly connected to the tragedy, Cope begins to suspect his sister might have survived. He reunites with his first love, Lucy Silverfield (Michelle Keegan, returning to the Coben universe after her massive success in Fool Me Once), to unravel years of lies, cover-ups, and family secrets.

items.headline: Nemesis season 2 gets a filming window and a new showrunner
items.summary: Gabriela Uribe takes over after Courtney A. Kemp stepped back when her Netflix deal expired and she signed with Apple. Filming is tentatively set for 15 March to 14 July 2027 in Los Angeles.
items.matters: no cast is confirmed, and the earliest realistic release is late 2027, with early 2028 more likely.
items.body:
Following a major showrunner shakeup, Netflix has now finally eyed a filming window for the return of Coltrane Wilder and Isaiah Stiles.

It’s been nearly five months since Netflix renewed Nemesis, and we’ve finally got some good news on when production will get going. The second season of the Los Angeles cat-and-mouse thriller is now set to begin filming in March 2027, although the dates mean fans are in for a long wait to see Coltrane Wilder and Isaiah Stiles go at it again.

Netflix officially renewed Nemesis for season 2 on June 30th, around six weeks after the first season debuted on May 14th, 2026. The show was a strong performer out of the gate, pulling in 7.1 million views in its first few days and charting in the top 10 in 83 countries.

Since then, though, things have been quiet on the production front, and the only major news was a big shakeup behind the scenes, with reports in July that co-creator Courtney A. Kemp would be stepping back from day-to-day showrunning duties after her exclusive Netflix deal expired and she signed a new deal with Apple.

According to new production listings, Nemesis season 2 is tentatively scheduled to begin filming on March 15th, 2027 and wrap on July 14th, 2027. As always with filming dates, these are highly subject to change.

That’s a four-month shoot, and, just as with the first season, production will take place in Los Angeles. That’ll be welcome news for the city’s crews. Kemp and co-creator Tani Marole were very vocal about the importance of filming in L.A. for season 1, describing the city as a character in the show and keeping a 200-plus local crew employed in the aftermath of the L.A. fires. Nemesis remains one of only a handful of Netflix scripted series shooting in Los Angeles, alongside the likes of The Lincoln Lawyer, Forever and Nobody Wants This.

If the March date sounds familiar, it’s because Nemesis joins another Netflix favorite in getting back in front of cameras that month. Just yesterday, we reported that The Diplomat season 5 will begin filming on March 9th, which also pushes that show’s release into 2028.

Following Kemp’s exit from day-to-day duties, we now know who’s taking the reins. According to the Writers Guild of America’s directory, Gabriela Uribe is the showrunner for Nemesis season 2, and she’s also an executive producer. Kemp and Tani Marole remain on board as executive producers.

items.headline: Netflix confirms Tokyo Swindlers season 2, with filming under way
items.summary: Go Ayano and Etsushi Toyokawa return, and Hitoshi One is back as director and screenwriter.
items.matters: Netflix has given no release date, and with filming only starting this autumn the new season is unlikely before 2027.
items.body:
Three months after we first reported the renewal, Netflix has made it official: Go Ayano and Etsushi Toyokawa are back, and cameras are already rolling.

It’s taken more than two years, but Netflix has finally confirmed that Tokyo Swindlers is returning for a second season. Go Ayano and Etsushi Toyokawa will reprise their roles as Takumi Tsujimoto and Harrison Yamanaka, with Hitoshi One back as both director and screenwriter.

If this sounds familiar, that’s because it is. Back in August, we covered a report from Japanese outlet Tokyo Sports that claimed Tokyo Swindlers, Yu Yu Hakusho, and Sanctuary had all been quietly renewed, with filming due to begin in the fall. Netflix didn’t respond to our requests for comment at the time, but today’s announcement confirms the first of those three.

Released in July 2024, the series spent six consecutive weeks at No. 1 on Netflix Japan’s weekly series top 10, something no title had managed since the charts launched in the country. It stayed in the Japanese top 10 for 22 weeks in total. Globally, it spent five consecutive weeks in the Non-English Series top 10 and charted in 15 countries.

Officially, not much. Netflix is keeping plot details under wraps, saying only that more will be revealed soon.

The announcement came with a first-look image showing a dimly lit room that looks a lot like Harrison’s lair. A map of a city sits in the middle of a desk, surrounded by stacks of cash.

Ko Shinjo, who wrote the original novel, offered the biggest hint about where things are heading:

Does a person who has pulled off one big con ever feel satisfied? Probably not. Human desire knows no limits. Searching for something beyond money alone, they will aim for an even bigger, even harder con. When I learned that a new season of Tokyo Swindlers series was being made, it struck me as oddly fitting. Once you’ve gotten a taste of it, you don’t walk away so easily. It seems that this time, too, an enormous plot of land (a target) is in play.

As a reminder, the Tokyo Sports report from August suggested the new season would dig into the origins of Harrison Yamanaka. That remains unconfirmed.

What’s on Netflix has also learned of two sequences that were scheduled to shoot between October 26th and 28th. The first was a politicians’ party scene filmed in Makuhari. items.headline: Worth watching this week: Steps, Netflix Animation's Cinderella retelling told from the stepsisters' side
items.summary: Ali Wong and Stephanie Hsu voice Lilith and Margot, with Amanda Seyfried as Cinderella, and it landed on Netflix on 20 November.
items.matters: TheWrap calls it "actually a very good kids movie" despite a shaky plot, and What's on Netflix gave it 4 out of 5.
items.body:
Good news, everybody! We’ve been keeping score and as of today, with the release of Alyce Tzue and John Ripa’s “Steps,” it’s official: There are more revisionist fairy tales than the so-called “real” ones.

It’s ironic, if you think about it. So many children’s movies are about poking holes in the Brothers Grimm’s stories — and while we’re at it, Aesop’s many Fables — that messing with the formula is now the formula. It’s not a shock when the villain of “Sleeping Beauty” gets her own lucrative movie franchise, and it’s not the least bit weird when Hansel and Gretel grow up to become butt-kicking witch hunters. Kenneth Branagh played it relatively straight when he remade Disney’s “Cinderella” in 2015, but even that film acknowledged that a “wicked step mother” is a one-dimensional concept, and falling in love in seconds is not what anyone seriously considers love.

You’d be hard pressed to find any classic fairy tale that doesn’t need at least some finagling to become relevant to modern audiences, and since those tales were, themselves, constantly evolving over time, nobody can claim films like “Steps” are an aberration. They’re just what fairy tales are these days, and “Steps,” a lively and amusing and character-driven new animated take on “Cinderella,” proves we’re better off for it.

“Steps” begins with Lilith (Ali Wong), Cinderella’s so called “evil” stepsister, telling the audience the original story was a smear campaign. In reality, Lilith and her little sister Margot (Stephanie Hsu) were, along with their mother, immigrants from East Asia, and their bad reputation was fueled by racism and classism.

When they meet their new stepsister Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried), she’s an impossibly kind young girl who loves cleaning the house and talking to animals, and they take an immediate shine to each other. But an early traumatic incident occurs, Cinderella chooses to side with the popular children over her stepsisters, and a rift develops. It only gets bigger when their father dies and the town completely turns on Lilith’s side of the family. Poor Cinderella, everyone says, having to live with those monsters.

So Lilith does what any teenager would do: She goes to Hot Topic. Or, since Hot Topic hasn’t been invented yet, it’s probably more accurate to say she invents Hot Topic. She’s ahead of her time, so nobody notices she’s a total style icon, but she embraces her outsider status and makes it her whole identity.

It takes a lot of contrivances to get the plot going, but in a nutshell: Lilith is furious when she finds out Cinderella has a Fairy Godmother…

items.headline: Commission accepts Temu's five-measure DSA action plan (26 October)
items.summary: Temu will run a platform-specific risk analysis, use reliable metrics for its mitigations, review its content moderation and recommender systems for amplification of illegal goods, and examine seller manipulation. This follows a May 2026 non-compliance decision with a €200m fine.
items.matters: Temu's interim risk assessment is due by 30 November, so expect the next step this week. For marketplace teams the five measures show what the Commission accepts as remediation: metrics-backed mitigation and recommender audits.
items.body:
The European Commission has accepted Temu's action plan to comply with the Digital Services Act (DSA) and tackle the availability of illegal products online.

The company will carry out a platform-specific risk analysis. It will also use reliable metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of the mitigation measures put in place in reducing the risk of dissemination of illegal content.

The platform will assess the limitations of its content moderation and analyse whether, and how, its recommender systems may amplify the spread of illegal goods. Additionally, Temu will examine the influence of intentional manipulation and amplification of illegal items, including by sellers exploiting Temu's features to spread potentially illegal listings.

The company now has four months to conduct an interim risk assessment that covers a six-month period, until 30 November 2026, to ensure the implementation of the measures of the action plan.

The action plan is another example of how the DSA is enhancing consumer protection online and limiting the spread of illegal products in Europe. The action plan was submitted following a non-compliance decision in May 2026, in which the Commission found that Temu had failed to comply with its risk assessment obligations, and issued a €200 million fine.

items.headline: EDPB adopts final DSA–GDPR interplay guidelines and a five-step fining methodology (adopted 21 September; fining text consulted until 13 November)
items.summary: the fining guidelines say minor infringements generally get a reprimand, while non-minor ones carry a strong presumption of a fine. They come with 14 worked examples.
items.matters: intermediary services that process personal data must read DSA and GDPR together, and should be clear whether they act as controller or processor, since liability follows that role. The fining text may still change after the consultation.
items.body:
Brussels, 21 September – During its latest plenary, the EDPB has adopted guidelines on the application of the power to impose administrative fines in relation to other corrective powers under the GDPR and the final version of its guidelines on interplay between the Digital Service Act (DSA) and the GDPR.

The new EDPB guidelines are a major step in further aligning how Data Protection Authorities decide whether an administrative fine should be imposed, either on its own or alongside other corrective measures.

The GDPR significantly increased the corrective powers of DPAs, with fines serving as an important instrument for effective enforcement. The guidelines reaffirm our commitment to providing greater clarity and ensuring the consistent application of the GDPR across Europe.

Data Protection Authorities (DPAs) should follow a five-step methodology when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine:

The guidelines also provide an overview of the corrective powers within the remit of national DPAs and explain their purpose, scope, and how they relate to one another. Corrective measures include warnings, reprimands, orders, limitations (including bans), and the withdrawal of certification.

The Board also provides 14 practical examples illustrating how DPAs can assess the specifics of a case and decide which corrective measures should be imposed, if any.

The guidelines will be subject to public consultation until 13 November 2026, providing stakeholders with the opportunity to comment and give feedback.

After public consultation, the EDPB adopted the final version of its guidelines on the interplay between the DSA and the GDPR. The guidelines support the consistent application of both legal acts, particularly where DSA provisions concern the processing of personal data by intermediary service providers and refer to concepts and definitions laid down in the GDPR.

* These Guidelines replace the WP29 guidelines on the application and setting of administrative fines for the purposes of the Regulation 2016/679 and complement the previously adopted guidelines on the calculation of administrative fines under the GDPR, which rather focus on the methodology for calculating the amount of an administrative fine.

items.headline: ProPublica on carbon capture
items.summary: Katie Worth's piece (21 November, about 1,500 words, roughly 7 minutes) asks why climate models and net-zero pledges lean on carbon capture and storage when only 12 large geologic storage projects have been built in three decades and at least seven underperformed or failed. It also reports that models assume capture rates of up to 92% and treat underground storage as nearly unlimited.
